ligament of head of femur: Ligament running from the fovea of the femoral head to the acetabular notch; the artery within it is important for supplying the femoral head in children.
ligamenta flava: Ligaments joining adjacent laminae, yellow because of their elastic fibres; in lumbar puncture resistance is felt as the needle passes through them.
limbus of sphenoid: Posterior edge of the jugum of the sphenoid.
linea alba: Fibrous band from the xiphoid to the symphysis where the aponeuroses of the three flat abdominal muscles fuse in the midline; wider above the umbilicus, it gives a bloodless route for surgical incisions.
linea aspera: Rough line on the back of the femoral shaft; the adductors and the vasti attach to it.
lingual surface of tooth: Surface of a tooth facing the tongue.
long head of biceps brachii: Head arising from the supraglenoid tubercle and passing through the shoulder joint; its tendon runs in the intertubercular sulcus, and rupture produces the 'Popeye' sign.
long head of biceps femoris: Hamstring head arising from the ischial tuberosity; extends the hip and flexes the knee. Tibial nerve.
long head of triceps brachii: Arises from the infraglenoid tubercle; it separates the triangular and quadrangular spaces. It also extends the shoulder.
long limb of incus: Long limb of the incus extending downwards; it runs parallel to the handle of the malleus.
long plantar ligament: The longest tarsal ligament, from the lower surface of the calcaneus to the cuboid and metatarsal bases; it roofs the canal of the fibularis longus tendon and supports the lateral arch.
longissimus capitis muscle: Part of longissimus inserting into the mastoid process; extends the head and turns it to the same side.
longissimus colli muscle: Cervical part of the longissimus column.
longissimus thoracis muscle: Trunk part of the middle and longest column of erector spinae.
longus capitis muscle: Prevertebral muscle from the transverse processes of C3–C6 to the basilar part of the occipital bone; flexes the head forwards.
longus colli muscle: Prevertebral muscle in front of the vertebral bodies from the anterior tubercle of the atlas to T3; flexes the neck forwards.
lower canine: Tooth at the corner of the mouth with the longest root; tears food.
lower first molar tooth: The first permanent tooth to erupt (age 6); it has a broad chewing surface and two roots.
lower first premolar: Premolar with two cusps; begins crushing food.
lower lateral incisor: Single-rooted incisor next to the central incisor.
lower medial incisor: Sharp-edged, single-rooted middle front tooth; cuts food by biting. It erupts at 6–8 years in the permanent dentition.
lower second molar tooth: Second molar erupting around age 12; it grinds food.
lower second premolar: Second premolar; usually single-rooted, with no counterpart in the milk teeth (it replaces the milk molars).
lumbrical muscles of foot: Four small muscles arising from the flexor digitorum longus tendons; they flex the MTP joints.
lumbrical muscles of hand: Four small muscles from the deep flexor tendons to the extensor hood; they flex the MCP and extend the IP joints. The 1st–2nd are supplied by the median nerve, the 3rd–4th by the ulnar nerve.
lunate bone: Half-moon-shaped bone in the middle of the proximal row; the most commonly dislocated carpal bone, and its anterior dislocation can compress the median nerve in the carpal tunnel. Its avascular necrosis is Kienböck's disease.
lunate surface: Crescent-shaped articular surface of the acetabulum; the cartilage-covered part in contact with the femoral head.
lunotriquetral interosseous ligament: Joins the lunate and triquetrum; a VISI deformity develops when it tears.
major alar cartilage: U-shaped cartilage shaping the tip of the nose and the rims of the nostrils; made up of medial and lateral crura.
malleolar fossa: Fossa on the posteromedial surface of the lateral malleolus; the posterior talofibular ligament attaches to it.
malleolar groove of fibula: Groove behind the lateral malleolus; the tendons of the fibular muscles pass through it.
malleolar groove of tibia: Groove behind the medial malleolus; the tibialis posterior and FDL tendons pass through it.
malleus: The outermost ossicle, attached to the eardrum; its handle (manubrium) is embedded in the inner surface of the drum, and tensor tympani attaches to it.
mandible: The only movable bone of the face; its condyles form the temporomandibular joint with the temporal bone. The inferior alveolar nerve runs in the mandibular canal.
mandibular symphysis: Site where the two halves of the mandible fuse in the midline after birth.
manubrium of sternum: Upper part of the sternum; articulates with the clavicles and the 1st costal cartilages, and bears the jugular notch on its upper border.
masseter: Runs from the zygomatic arch to the angle of the mandible; one of the strongest muscles for its weight, it closes the jaw. Masseteric nerve (V3).
masseteric fascia: Fascia covering masseter, continuous with the parotid fascia.
mastoid angle of parietal bone: Posteroinferior angle facing the mastoid region.
mastoid border of occipital bone: Border that articulates with the mastoid part of the temporal bone.
mastoid notch: Notch on the medial side of the mastoid process; the posterior belly of digastric arises here.
mastoid process: Projection felt behind the ear; it is filled with air cells and SCM attaches to it.
maxilla: Paired bone forming the upper jaw, the front of the hard palate, the floor of the orbit and the lateral wall of the nasal cavity; it contains the maxillary sinus, the largest paranasal sinus.
maxillary dental arch: Upper dental arch; it carries 16 permanent teeth.
maxillary surface of greater wing: Surface of the greater wing facing the pterygopalatine fossa; the foramen rotundum opens here.
medial border of scapula: Medial border facing the spine; the rhomboids and serratus anterior attach to it.
medial condyle of femur: Medial condyle of the femur; it is longer and reaches lower than the lateral condyle, producing the carrying angle.
medial condyle of tibia: Medial condyle of the tibia; semimembranosus attaches to its back.
medial cuneiform bone: The largest of the three cuneiforms; articulates with the 1st metatarsal and gives attachment to tibialis anterior and fibularis longus.
medial epicondyle of femur: Prominence on the medial condyle; the medial collateral ligament attaches to it.
medial epicondyle of humerus: Medial epicondyle of the humerus; common origin of the forearm flexors, with the ulnar nerve passing behind it.
medial femoral intermuscular septum: Fascial wall separating the anterior and medial thigh compartments.
medial head of flexor hallucis brevis: Medial head of flexor hallucis brevis
Head attaching to the medial sesamoid.
